newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dowa,S'tomo join Mexico zinc deposit study.
newsitem.headline: Dowa,S'tomo join Mexico zinc deposit study.

text.p: Dowa Mining Co said on Thursday it and Sumitomo Corp have agreed with Mexico's Industrias Penoles SA de CV to conduct a joint feasibility study of a zinc/lead/silver ore reserve in Mexico.
The company said drilling already carried out at the Rey de Plata site in Guerrero state revealed a reserve of more than three million tonnes of ore.
Dowa, one of Japan's leading zinc refiners, said the ore is similar to the complex kurokko ore at Mexico's Tizapa mine, which is run jointly by the same three companies.
The Tizapa mine currently produces 1.000 tonnes of ore per day and is scheduled to expand to 1,600 tonnes per day within the next year.
Dowa said that, pending the results of the feasibility study, the partners hope to develop Rey de Plata with initial production of 1,000 tonnes of ore per day.
The company added that Rey de Plata is expected to yield grades similar to Tizapa's 10 to 11 percent zinc/lead and 314 grammes per tonne of silver.

Dowa said the Rey de Plata project, combined with the expansion at Tizapa, would lift to over 50 percent the portion of its zinc concentrates which are supplied directly from mines in which it holds an equity stake.
Dowa plans to produce about 90,000 tonnes of refined zinc in the business year through April 1997.
